title: The two ordinary exchange/projection leg transposes
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $k,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. For a $k$-scheme $T$, put $D(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the ordinary unbounded derived category on its small pro-etale site. For a scheme map $u$ use $P_u=Lu^*$, $R_u=Ru_*$ and the canonical adjunction $P_u\dashv R_u$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$. Let $B,Y,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $a:Y\to B$, $b:Z\to B$ be separated finite-type morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and form $C=Y\times_BZ$ with projections $r:C\to Y$, $t:C\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. All tensors and symmetries are the derived tensor and signed symmetry of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the canonical tensor comparisons $\mu_u$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] and the square comparison $\theta:P_tP_b\xrightarrow{\sim}P_rP_a$ obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. For arbitrary $H\in D(Y)$ and $J\in D(Z)$ put $F=R_aH$, $G=R_bJ$, $T=P_rH$, $Q=P_bF\otimes_A^LJ$, and $E=T\otimes_A^LP_tJ$. Let $x:P_bF\to R_tT$ and $\pi_{u;M,N}$ be exactly the counit-defined ordinary exchange and projection maps of [def-exchange-projection]. Define
$$v=\pi_{t;T,J}\circ(x\otimes1_J):Q\to R_tE,$$
$$w=R_b(\sigma_{J,P_bF})\circ\pi_{b;J,F}\circ\sigma_{F,G}:F\otimes_A^LG\to R_bQ.$$
For an arrow $h:M\to R_uN$, define $\widehat h=\varepsilon_{u,N}\circ P_u(h)$. Then the two identities, with their actual source comparisons included, are
$$\widehat v=\bigl((P_r\varepsilon_{a,H}\circ\theta_F)\otimes1_{P_tJ}\bigr)\circ\mu_{t;P_bF,J}:P_tQ\to E,$$
$$\widehat w=(1_{P_bF}\otimes\varepsilon_{b,J})\circ\mu_{b;F,G}:P_b(F\otimes_A^LG)\to Q.$$
Both hold for arbitrary unbounded $H,J$; properness and invertibility of exchange or projection are not assumptions.

proof.text:
Write $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$. The adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] has inverse hom-bijection $d\mapsto R_u(d)\eta_u$. Its transpose is $h\mapsto\varepsilon_uP_u(h)$: naturality of $\varepsilon_u$ gives $\varepsilon_uP_uR_u(d)P_u\eta_u=d\varepsilon_uP_u\eta_u=d$ by the triangle identity. Therefore [def-exchange-projection], which defines exchange and projection by precisely these adjunct formulas, gives
$$\widehat x=P_r(\varepsilon_{a,H})\theta_F,\qquad \widehat{\pi_{u;M,N}}=(\varepsilon_{u,M}\otimes1_{P_uN})\mu_{u;R_uM,N}.$$
Here the comparison $\mu_u$ inside the projection map of [def-exchange-projection] is the ambient ringed-topos tensor-pullback comparison, and [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] states that at finite level its $\mu_u$ is exactly this canonical comparison for the morphism of ringed topoi induced by $u$; so the displayed $\mu$ is the $\mu$ of the statement. These formulas are in the ordinary unbounded categories; neither map is inverted.

proof.text:
Expand $v$ and its transpose using step 1. Naturality of $\mu_t$ in [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], applied to $x:P_bF\to R_tT$ and $1_J$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\widehat v&=(\varepsilon_{t,T}\otimes1)\mu_{t;R_tT,J}P_t(x\otimes1_J)\\
&=(\varepsilon_{t,T}\otimes1)(P_t x\otimes1)\mu_{t;P_bF,J}\\
&=((P_r\varepsilon_{a,H}\circ\theta_F)\otimes1_{P_tJ})\mu_{t;P_bF,J}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality substitutes the projection transpose from step 1; the last uses $\varepsilon_{t,T}P_t x=\widehat x$. The comparison on the source is retained, so this is exactly the first asserted identity.

source.place: Tag 0E48, label remark-compatible-with-diagram; equation-projection-formula-map immediately preceding it; explicit adjunction calculation

proof.text:
Put $s=\sigma_{J,P_bF}$. Naturality of the counit gives $\varepsilon_{b,Q}P_bR_b(s)=s\varepsilon_{b,J\otimes P_bF}$. Expanding $w$ and using step 1 yields
$$\widehat w=s(\varepsilon_{b,J}\otimes1_{P_bF})\mu_{b;G,F}P_b(\sigma_{F,G}).$$
The signed-symmetry compatibility of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] replaces the final two factors by $\sigma_{P_bF,P_bG}\mu_{b;F,G}$. Naturality of tensor symmetry gives
$$s(\varepsilon_{b,J}\otimes1_{P_bF})=(1_{P_bF}\otimes\varepsilon_{b,J})\sigma_{P_bG,P_bF}.$$
Since $\sigma_{P_bG,P_bF}\sigma_{P_bF,P_bG}=1$, this proves $\widehat w=(1_{P_bF}\otimes\varepsilon_{b,J})\mu_{b;F,G}$. Symmetry is the signed derived symmetry throughout; its involutivity cancels the two swaps for arbitrary complexes.
